data.name: Bholanath
data.gender_notes: Bholanath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bholanath is a compound name from 'Bhola', meaning foolish or simple, and 'Nath', meaning lord. In Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva is often referred to as Bholanath due to his playful and mischievous nature. The name Bholanath carries the meaning “Lord of Foolishness” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bholanath usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of foolishness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embraces the foolishness of human nature, encouraging us to let go of our ego and connect with the divine.
data.etymology: Bholanath belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Foolishness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bholanath total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Bholanath" is deeply rooted in the rich heritage of Hindu culture and mythology. The playful and mischievous aspect of Lord Shiva as Bholanath reflects the entire spectrum of his complex personality - from the transcendental and detached to the passionate and engaged. This representation adds to the depth and complexity of Hindu deities and their relationships with their followers.
data.spiritual_significance: Symbolically, Bholanath represents the divine energy that exists beyond human understanding and the limitations of logic and reason. This name underscores the belief that the divine is not confined to principles or dogma, but rather exists in a state of playful and unpredictable love for its creation. It encourages followers to approach the divine with childlike faith, trusting in the wisdom and love of the universe, even when it may seem foolish or simple to the human mind.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bholanath translates to 'Lord of the Foolish'. This name signifies the divine power that lovingly accepts and uplifts even the most careless and foolish souls towards spiritual growth. It emphasizes that divine grace is not limited to the wise and virtuous, but extends to all, irrespective of their stage in life.
